entries.test: Whether AI industry leaders such as Jensen Huang and Boris Cherny publicly promoted 'loops' (LLMs prompting LLMs) around June 2026.
entries.note: This is an earlier prediction he now says has come true. The 'desperate attempt' motive and the revenue aim he 'imagines' cannot be tested.
The main claim is a motive ('no other ideas'). The trillion-dollar spending figure could be checked on its own.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI and Anthropic are reported as the largest individual cloud customers of Microsoft, Google and Amazon, bringing meaningful new revenue.
entries.note: The 'mistaken belief' part is hedged with 'I imagine' and is about private beliefs.
'Nobody' is hyperbole, and blaming a narrative for stock moves has no shared test.

entries.test: Whether Baseten runs its compute on rented hyperscaler capacity rather than infrastructure it owns, according to company disclosures or reporting.
entries.note: 'Directly into the pockets' of hyperscalers overstates it: not all of the raise goes to compute.

entries.test: The reported cost of Microsoft's Inflection/Suleyman deal and whether Microsoft's earnings break out AI revenue.
entries.note: 'Universally-loathed' and 'mid-tier' are rhetoric. The deal cost and the revenue disclosure can be checked.

entries.test: Whether Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta and Amazon released OpenClaw-related products, whether OpenAI hired OpenClaw's founder, and survey data on public awareness of OpenClaw.
entries.note: '99%' is likely hyperbole. The 'which is why' link makes little sense causally.
This explains why people hold their beliefs, which public evidence cannot settle.
This is about the companies' motives and what they would have done otherwise.

entries.test: Whether hyperscalers or others fully fund OpenAI's and Anthropic's infrastructure, and whether other firms (Google, Meta, xAI) train models and serve inference at comparable scale.
entries.note: The proposition bundles several separate sub-claims.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI's and Anthropic's reported losses and infrastructure have been funded by outside capital from hyperscalers and VCs rather than by operating cash flow.
entries.note: 'Infinite resources' is hyperbole. The plain reading is that both depend on outside funding.
This is a counterfactual about a hypothetical disappearance.

entries.test: AWS's cumulative losses before profitability compared with OpenAI's and Anthropic's reported losses.
entries.note: The 'more useful' comparison is a value judgment. Only the loss comparison can be checked.

entries.test: Whether major AI labs' and startups' subscription plans were priced below the cost of serving them, according to reported financials.
entries.note: 'Every' is very broad, and the 'assuming' part is about private beliefs.

entries.test: The release dates of Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex coding agent, and whether OpenAI and Anthropic cited scaling-law research to justify pre-training spend.
entries.note: 'Infinite gains' overstates what the scaling-law papers said.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI and Anthropic both offered free API credits or free trial periods for competing coding products in 2026.
entries.note: The stated aim (convincing VCs and markets) is a motive and cannot be tested.
This is framed with 'perhaps' as one of several possibilities. The 98% figure is assumed rather than asserted.
'Only exists' and 'deliberately obfuscating' are claims about intent.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI's audited or disclosed financials show inference costs classified under sales and marketing, or a restatement of its cost of revenue.
entries.note: The decisive evidence may not be public yet. The second half is hedged with 'I believe'.
